title: driver-turso remote: a declared index skipped because a key column never materializes (a misspelt or formula column) is logged through the warn diagnostic sink, not the durability sink, so a skipped UNIQUE stays quiet (#20432 on the remote face)
body:
Filing gate: **① a product defect with a named landing site**. Finding class **(a)**, the durability-log-level rule. `reach:` is a remote Turso datasource (`TursoDriver` in remote mode) whose object declares `indexes: [{ fields: ['statsu'], unique: true }]` on a table whose column is `status`, at `syncSchema`. **Derived at source**, not driven, on PR #20519's head `87f6c0bfd` (identical on `main` for this file). The at-tier contract review of PR #20519 escalated it as a follow-up (record 5881320756, ③ c).

Filed by the `domain:engine` execution seat 1 (`session_01N8TPEsoJxPsdSdNKGnNGEN`, `os-warren`). ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading belong to triage. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens

`packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts`, the remote index sync (about `:2453–2461`): when a declared index's key column is not materialized, it writes

> `[RemoteTransport] skipping declared index "NAME" on "TABLE" — column(s) not materialized: COLUMN`

through `this.diagnosticSink`, and `continue`s. `TursoDriver` wires that sink to `this.logger.warn` (`turso-driver.ts:1609`).

- A declared **UNIQUE** index skipped this way leaves uniqueness unenforced. Every write keeps succeeding, logged at **warn**.
- The same transport already has a second, **durability** sink (#8413, documented beside `diagnosticSink` at about `:1230`) for exactly this class: "a declared UNIQUE index that could not be created … every write keeps succeeding". The duplicate-row case goes there. The not-materialized case does not.

## Why it is its own card

#20432 (PR #20519) makes the local face (`SqlDriver.syncDeclaredIndexes`, which turso local and sqlite-wasm inherit) log this skip at **error** through `logDurabilityFailure`, and report it in drift as `unbuildable_index`. The remote face keeps its own copy of the skip, which that card's claim did not cover. The remote face also refuses drift detection, so `os migrate plan` cannot show the skipped index there either.

## Suggested shape (⛔ not a ruling)

- Route the remote skip through the durability sink, at error, naming the unenforced constraint for a `unique` index, as the local face now does.
- Keep the plain (non-unique) index skip on whichever sink the durability rule assigns it.
- Pin it with a remote-transport test on a misspelt and a `formula` key column.

## Dedupe

`search_issues`, run by this seat in `objectstack-ai/objectstack`, open and closed: "turso RemoteTransport skipping declared index column not materialized unique index warn diagnostic sink durability" gives 16 hits. #17609 (remote never materialized object-level `indexes`, closed), #20424, #19845 and #19823 are other remote-face defects. None is this.

Dedupe words: `turso remote skipped declared index warn` · `RemoteTransport not materialized unique index log level` · `diagnosticSink durability sink skipped index`
